transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you're all aware, robotic palletizer P-4 stopped during the morning shift, and we have a manual palletizing station available in the finished-goods warehouse as a temporary alternative. We also have an urgent outbound order scheduled for the end of the week, so we need to move quickly on a recovery plan. As plant manager, I'll be making the binding decision on the recovery method and any controls attached to it, but I want input from production, maintenance, logistics, and safety before we proceed. The recovery plan needs to document three things before we execute: the maintenance work required, shipment staging requirements, and energy-isolation controls. Let's start by hearing from each of you on what you know and what we need to consider.

The good news is that the replacement seal is stocked on site, so we don't need to wait on parts. I should note that the full maintenance report is still awaiting my supervisor's signoff, but the inspection findings are solid and I'm confident in these numbers.
